stumbles.why: "Settle" is never defined. It isn't clear how a 5% error budget turns probabilities into settled hits, or which Jev setup the 24.5% comes from.

stumbles.quote: Five of 44 triad hits were real tics, as were 5 of 43 participle hits and 16 of 18 negation-first hits.
stumbles.why: The terms triad, participle and negation-first are unexplained lint rules. The counts also appear to be drawn from the 261 agreed hits, which the text doesn't say.

stumbles.quote: It had done well on routing questions, so I was hopeful.
stumbles.why: This refers to earlier Jev work that the text never describes.

stumbles.quote: An Opus judge and a Sonnet judge agreed on 261 of them (87%), and 35.2% of those 261 were real tics.
stumbles.why: It isn't clear how "real tic" was decided. It might be the judges' shared label, but that is not stated. Also, 5+5+16 is 26 out of 105 hits, which doesn't obviously connect to the 35.2%.

point: Jev, a small calibrated decision model, was tested as a reviewer of lint hits for tic patterns. It did not beat a simple per-category baseline by much and settled only 24.5% of hits against a 50% bar, so it was not added to the review process.
